inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-09-30: 109.9M shares outstanding (141.4M issued less 31.5M treasury, FY2026 10-K balance sheet) plus 0.5M dilutive awards (FY2026 diluted 112.0M less basic 111.5M weighted average) = 110.4M. Cover-page count 109.76M at 2026-10-31. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging dilution as well would double-count). Rockwell is an active repurchaser ($1,256M FY2026, $425M FY2025), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.debt_note: Total debt at 2026-09-30 (FY2026 10-K balance sheet) = short-term debt 709 (707 commercial paper) + current long-term debt 2 + long-term debt 2,569. The Metrics.csv TotalDebt column omits commercial paper; this DCF uses the full figure. Operating lease liabilities (272 non-current) excluded: US GAAP operating lease cost already sits inside operating income/EBITDA (treatment B by construction).
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2026 as reported: cash from operations 1,958 less capex 257 = 1,701 (after interest paid). Includes $108M of non-recurring IEEPA tariff refunds and related interest received in Q4; underlying reported FCF ~1,593 and underlying owner FCF ~1,501. The forward build does not carry the refund.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income $16M (incl. $5M on tariff refunds) not stripped: Rockwell is net-debt (2.8B), so no cash pile is added to EV and the double-count rule does not apply.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement, share-based compensation expense 92 (85 FY2025, 100 FY2024). No separate tax-withholding-on-net-share-settlement line is disclosed; awards are largely options settled for cash proceeds ($95M FY2026), so equity-award taxes are immaterial and not added.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 purchases of treasury stock (financing activities), 3.1M shares at $401 average; FY2025 425. $673M remained on the authorization at 2026-09-30.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), beta ~1.1 for a large-cap quality industrial, ERP 4.5-5% -> cost of equity ~9.3%; debt ~6% of capital at ~4.5% pre-tax (3.6% after tax) -> WACC ~9.0%. Held identical across scenarios: cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows (bear carries an FY2023-24 style destock), not stacked on the discount rate. UNCHANGED in the 2026-11-19 update: no rate or leverage evidence since October moves a 9.0% rate by a rounding step.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost is inside operating income and EBITDA already (treatment B); lease liabilities excluded from net debt; lease_cost_pct_path 0 to avoid a second charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest $2M at 2026-09-30 after the Sensia JV dissolution (57 at FY2025); immaterial, no deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 'Operating company, cyclical: industrials'), 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted, end-of-year discounting; same model as the 2026-10-02 first valuation. UPDATE 2026-11-19 on the FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-11-12) and the 2026-11-05 earnings release with FY2027 guidance. FY0 is now FY2026 actual: base_revenue 8,989 as reported, which is net of an $85M customer tariff refund accrual (underlying 9,074); the year-1 growth rates are on the reported base and so include the guide's ~1pt lap of that accrual and ~-1.5pt Sensia divestiture. Year 1 is FY2027, as before, so every later-year driver keeps its fiscal year. CHANGED: balance-sheet anchors; year-1 growth (guide reported +4.5-7.5%, organic +6-9%); EBITDA margin paths (a -2.6pp definitional correction, see ebitda_definition, partly offset by +1.3pp for the FY2026 actual and the FY2027 EPS guide); capex years 1-3 (FY2027 guide ~$400M against 257 in FY2026); cash tax years 1-2 (guide ~20%). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth years 2-10 in all scenarios (would move on a second year of organic growth above 6% or on orders/PMI rolling over); SBC 1.0% of sales (FY2026 actual 1.02%); D&A path (FY2026 actual 3.5%); capex from year 4 (would move if the $2B programme is extended); working-capital capture -15% (FY2026 working capital was a net inflow helped by payables and accruals, not a change in structure); WACC 9.0%; terminal growth and exit caps 13/16/19x; weights 25/50/25 (the stock sits later in the upswing after a third guidance step-up, which keeps the bear weight where it is). Not deducted, as before: legacy asbestos and environmental accruals in other liabilities; a pre-existing omission that slightly overstates value. Year-1 check: base FY2027 unlevered owner FCF ~1,497 (15.7% of sales) against a guide-implied ~1,496 (GAAP net income ~1,566 + D&A ~310 - capex 400 - working capital ~80 + after-tax interest ~100); FY2026 actual on the same basis ~1,597 including a working-capital inflow and capex of only 257. Working capital is negative capture (receivables + inventory exceed payables + contract liabilities).
inputs.ebitda_definition: Pre-SBC EBITDA = Enterprise operating profit (after corporate cost, before acquisition amortization) + depreciation + non-acquisition amortization + SBC. FY2026: 1,997 - 10 net tariff items + 183 + 11 + 92 = 2,273 = 25.1% of underlying sales 9,074; cross-check company Adjusted EBITDA 2,182 (24.3%, after SBC) + 92 = 2,274. FY2027 guide midpoint (adjusted EPS $15.00 on ~110.4M shares, ~20% tax, ~$125M net interest, sales ~9,528) implies ~26.1%. The Metrics.csv EBITDA column is NOT this measure: it is segment operating earnings + total D&A, which omits corporate and other (116) and adds acquisition amortization (120) back to a figure that already excludes it, overstating by ~2.6pp. The prior version's paths were anchored to that column.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.7% is in line with revenue 5.1% but EPS is only 1.6%: FY2021 EPS (11.58) was inflated by PTC mark-to-market gains, and book equity is held down by buybacks above earnings ($1,256M repurchased in FY2026 alone; equity fell 3,711 -> 3,554). Neither is a clean growth anchor; revenue 5yr CAGR (includes the Plex/Clearpath/Verve acquisitions and the Sensia exit) is selected, as before.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs now end at FY2026 (FY2023 and FY2021 bases). FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (FCF - SBC): 1,609 FY2026, 1,125 FY2023, 1,089 FY2021. FY2026 includes $108M of one-off tariff refunds; excluding it the owner-FCF CAGRs are ~10.1% (3yr) and ~6.6% (5yr). Revenue 3yr is flat because FY2023 was the post-shortage shipment peak. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR sits 0.2pp below reported, so SBC (~1% of revenue) is not consuming the growth.

base.narrative: Recovery runs through FY2027-28, then a mild mid-cycle pause (FY2029-30) before trend growth of ~4-5% fading to 3%; margin settles at ~26.2% pre-SBC EBITDA (FY2026 actual 25.1%, FY2027 guide ~26.1%), holding the software-mix gain but not extending it.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Year 1 at 26.1% is the FY2027 guide midpoint (adjusted EPS $15.00); it gives an FY2027 unlevered owner-FCF margin of ~15.7%, below FY2026's ~17.6% because capex steps up to ~$400M and working capital reverts to a cost of growth. Later years keep the prior path's shape on the corrected EBITDA definition and settle at 26.2%.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2025-26 recovery (FY2026 organic +8%, Software & Control +17% at a 33.8% segment margin, FY2027 guided to organic +6-9%) is real but cyclical: restocking and data-centre/semiconductor capex carry FY2027-28, then discrete-manufacturing capex pauses as it has every 4-5 years, before reshoring and the software mix restore ~4-5% growth fading to 3%. The margin gain is kept at about the guided FY2027 level (~26% pre-SBC EBITDA) but not extended; Lifecycle Services stays flat-ish after the Sensia exit and Intelligent Devices remains a hardware cyclical. Capex runs well above history through FY2029 on the $2B US manufacturing and digital-infrastructure programme, starting with ~$400M in FY2027 and the New Berlin greenfield campus.
scenario_narratives.bull: Reshoring and tariff-driven factory investment turn into a multi-year North American automation cycle with no meaningful downturn inside the horizon; AI-enabled FactoryTalk/digital-twin software and recurring ARR lift Software & Control to ~35% of sales at mid-30s segment margins, taking enterprise pre-SBC EBITDA to ~29.7%, about 3.5pp above the guided FY2027 level. Rockwell takes share from Siemens/Schneider in North American discrete and its installed-base switching costs convert the growth into durable aftermarket revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: The current upswing proves to be restocking: FY2027 comes in below the low end of guidance, then as in FY2023-24 distributors destock and manufacturing PMI rolls over, revenue falls ~9% over FY2028-29 and margins give back the software-mix gains under negative operating leverage (trough ~22% pre-SBC EBITDA against 21.2% in FY2024). Tariff and export-control volatility, China overcapacity and the larger diversified rivals' pricing keep recovery growth to 3-5% and the terminal margin at ~24.2%, below today's level, valued at a 13x cyclical exit. The New Berlin build is committed, so capex cannot fall as fast as sales.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED from the first valuation. Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default because Rockwell's revenue has a demonstrated 4-5 year boom-bust pattern (FY2021-22 boom, FY2023-24 destock) and the valuation date sits after two FY2026 guidance raises and a strong FY2027 guide, i.e. later in the upswing, not at a trough. Base 50% embeds one mild pause. Bull cut to 25% from 35% because it needs several independent things at once: no cyclical downturn for a decade, sustained reshoring capex, and software mix lifting enterprise margin a further ~3.5pp.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Rockwell is valued as a quality cyclical on an owner-FCF basis: SBC (~1% of revenue) fully expensed, share count flat and funded by buybacks, mid-cycle rather than peak margins capitalised at a 13-19x exit. The market price capitalises roughly 30x trailing underlying owner FCF (unlevered, excluding the one-off tariff refunds), which the model can only approach if the bull case's decade without a downturn and a further structural margin step-up both happen; the gap between price and weighted value is the price of that thesis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing: a FY2028-29 destock (bear) versus continued recovery swings near-term FCF by 25-30%
Software & Control margin durability: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly 5% of value
Terminal multiple: the cap binds in the base case, so a market willing to pay 20x+ for automation exposure sits outside the house basis
The $2B US investment programme lifts capex to ~4% of sales in FY2027 against a 2.2-2.8% history; if it runs longer than three years or fails to earn a return, base FCF is overstated
FY2026 cash flow flattered by $108M of IEEPA tariff refunds, of which $85M is owed back to customers in FY2027; export controls on industrial control technology to China
